question.text: Suppose that gold is being plated on to another metal in an electrolytic cell. The half-cell reaction producing the Au(s) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>A</mtext><mtext>u</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msubsup><mtext>l</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup><msup><mtext> +3e</mtext><mo>-</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><mtext>A</mtext><mtext>u</mtext><mfenced separators="|"><mtext>s</mtext></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>C</mtext><msup><mtext>l</mtext><mo>-</mo></msup></math> . If a 0.30 A current runs for 15.00 minute, what mass of Au(s) will be plated, assume all the electrons are used in the reduction of <math><mtext>A</mtext><mtext>u</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msubsup><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> ? The Faraday constant is 96485 <math><mrow><mrow><mtext>C</mtext></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mtext>m</mtext><mtext>o</mtext><mtext>l</mtext></mrow></mrow></math> and molar mass of Au is 197.

solution.text:
Mass of Au deposited = Number of Faraday passed × Eq. mass

=0.30×15×6096485×1973=0.184 g
